objects.name: Constellation 0.1.0-alpha.6 — reviewed local copy
objects.claim: One exact local-copy plan was independently reviewed, explicitly accepted, authorized once, executed under Docket custody, settled successfully, and followed by a read-only observation. An anonymous public-clone reproduction verified the retained evidence without repeating the provider call or effect.
objects.verified_by: the immutable alpha.6 manifest, qualification record, walkthrough, and anonymous public-clone verification
objects.promotion: This release is immutable. Operational burn-in, live notification delivery, cross-version restore, migration, rollback, and production consumer adoption require separate evidence.

objects.name: Alpha 2 — governed service start on two fresh Ubuntu 22.04 machines
objects.status: accepted Alpha 2 showing; published prerelease; not a general suite release
objects.claim: Six Ubuntu 22.04 packages (AG operator tools and systemd executor, Docket, Nightshift, NQ 0.2.0 and a Pulse support package) were installed from one published source-free bundle onto two fresh virtual machines. On the target, AG issued one exact one-use authority, Docket consumed the enrolled owner standing, kept custody of the single attempt, dispatched the signed envelope and settled success, and a fixed, previously inactive systemd service started. NQ on the target independently observed the unit loaded, active and running; NQ on the controller independently fetched the service's health endpoint and matched status, no-redirect and the shipped body hash. Pulse judged current support for exactly those two propositions. Two earlier setup attempts were refused before any authority was issued, and their records were kept.
objects.verified_by: showing m2-support-003, completed 2026-10-02 02:41 UTC: all 15 installed runtime executables on both machines matched the candidate bytes, the five component source commits matched their published dev/operator-beta refs, and the result record and records archive were published with the bundle and its digest
objects.promotion: This is a prerelease that shows one fixed scenario on two fresh machines, once. It is not aggregate health, effect causation, exactly-once execution, clock accuracy, general support-family adoption or a beta. The component repositories carry the exact source on their dev/operator-beta branches and have no new tags or releases; build reproduction is not claimed; NQ's UTC time quality is unqualified. Beta needs ordinary component release and promotion lifecycle, restart and outcome-unknown handling, durable install, upgrade, rollback and day-two operation, and a reviewed beta release.

objects.name: Observation profile, generation one, on one operator host
objects.status: installed and exercised 2026-10-01; acquisition failing closed since 18:49 UTC the same day
objects.claim: NQ 0.2.0, Monitor's host-posture runner and a Nightshift recurrence timer were installed from Ubuntu 22.04 packages as services on one production-adjacent operator host. Within the first hour the runner made real filesystem-capacity observations and published a status projection, NQ delivered one live Slack message that the owner received, and the timer ran one unattended recurrence tick. From 18:49 UTC NQ's per-invocation work exceeded the runner's fixed time bounds, and every cycle since has been refused and published as unknown, which is the runner's designed fail-closed response. The cause is in NQ: it validates the entire retained history on every store open, so cost grows without bound. The same mechanism was seen in an earlier sustained VM run.
objects.verified_by: the owner's dated installation record and its correction of 2026-10-02 03:05 UTC, summarized on the record page with host identity removed; package digests are listed there
objects.promotion: A bounded, watermarked validation path in NQ; a reinstall that stays healthy for a stated period and survives a reboot on the host; and the recurrence glue becoming a component contract rather than site-written configuration. No governed effect runs on that host, and nothing about it is a production claim.

objects.name: reviewed-local-copy/v1 — earlier Alpha 2 release candidate (2026-09-25), history
objects.status: historical release candidate; never accepted; superseded by the accepted Alpha 2 showing
objects.claim: Packaged builds of NQ, Maude, Nightshift, Pulse, AG, Docket, Switchyard and the App Server, with a setup kit, were installed into a fresh Debian 12 virtual machine from those artifacts alone. One reviewed and accepted occurrence settled successfully and wrote its file exactly once. Every requested refusal held: a wrong artifact digest, a repeated init, a stale review, an expired authorization, a second execution attempt, and acceptance of the wrong candidate. The review came from a local fixture standing in for the model provider, and the acceptance was performed by the test harness, not by a person.
objects.verified_by: clean-install run-004 on 2026-09-25: 31 pass, 0 fail, 0 not exercised, with setup kit 0.4.0. It reruns every earlier case, including a check that the evidence verifier shipped in the kit gives the same result inside the virtual machine as outside it and a replay of the settled evidence without the issuer's private key, and adds cases from the hostile review: the review's altered setup kits and substitute artifact were run against the new bundle and refused, and an already-installed NQ is now compared with the package file by file. An earlier upgrade-continuity run (run-002: 22 pass, 0 fail, 0 not exercised) upgraded an install of the previous kit to a second, test-only build and re-verified the first build's retained evidence, byte for byte; the upgrade code is unchanged in kit 0.4.0, so it was not rerun. Both run records are retained privately; the harness source is public on an unmerged branch.

evidence.label: the released alpha.6 profile it packages

objects.promotion: Closed. This candidate was never accepted and will not be released; the accepted Alpha 2 is the two-machine showing of 2026-10-02 on Ubuntu 22.04, built from different forward source lines. The record stays because the clean-install, newcomer, upgrade-continuity and hostile-review results remain evidence about the alpha.6 composition's packaging. The local trust boundary it found is still open and now described against Alpha 2 on the limits page. The two harness links point at a commit that is only on an unmerged site branch and will break if that branch is deleted.

objects.name: Indeterminate-effect demo (refund with a lost reply)
objects.status: cold-clone qualified; tagged public exhibit, not a Docket release
objects.claim: An agent reports a refund done after the reply was lost. Docket, built from source, records the attempt as indeterminate, sends nothing twice, and settles success or failure only on a separate observer's read of the provider's ledger. A second run with the request lost ends in failure under the same agent claim. Docket is real; the authorization signer (a stand-in reproducing AG's published test vector), the payment provider, the faulty network link and the agent are local stand-ins. Everything runs on one host under one clock.
objects.verified_by: run-003: an anonymous HTTPS clone of the demo source into a fresh Debian 12 virtual machine, with the network cut off for the build and the run; the demo exited 0 and its independent check passed 53 of 53 checks. The exhibit tag demo/indeterminate-effect-20260925 (eeb0534) carries the same demo code; only the README changed.
objects.promotion: The tag is a qualified public exhibit, not a Docket release or cohort promotion; the demo counts as part of Docket only once it is merged there. Independence holds because this demo's worker delegates reconcile to the observer; Docket does not pin that configuration, so it is not a general guarantee. Using AG itself, a remote provider, or several observers would each need separate evidence.

objects.name: Constellation Docket
objects.claim: Takes custody of one authorized attempt, dispatches an authority-neutral executor, and records settlement and reconciliation. Alpha.6 exercised its bounded local permission snapshot and local-copy executor path. Alpha 2 exercised enrolled owner-standing enforcement, attempt custody, signed dispatch and settlement across two machines (forward source 0c771e9b, published on dev/operator-beta).
objects.verified_by: the alpha.6 manifest and qualification record at the exact pinned public revision; the Alpha 2 showing of 2026-10-02 at the published forward source
objects.promotion: The profile is narrow; it does not establish production hardening or arbitrary executor compatibility.

objects.name: Constellation AG
objects.claim: Checks whether exact automated work is admissible and grants bounded one-use authority for one specific run. It does not execute work or infer permission from a provider response. Alpha 2 exercised one-use authority for a signed systemd service start on a separate machine (forward source f21b2431, published on dev/operator-beta).
objects.verified_by: the alpha.6 one-use authorization and public evidence-reader checks; the Alpha 2 showing of 2026-10-02 at the published forward source
objects.promotion: No family-wide or production maturity is claimed.

objects.name: Constellation NQ
objects.claim: Evaluates retained evidence under named profiles and keeps missing, stale, unavailable, or uncertain results visible. Its results do not authorize an effect.
objects.verified_by: alpha.2 through alpha.6 profiles, the Alpha 2 showing's fresh unit and HTTP observations, and the operator-host installation record
objects.promotion: One live Slack delivery was observed on 2026-10-01 with the owner confirming receipt; that is one message, not qualified delivery. Sustained acquisition over a growing store failed on the operator host because NQ validates its whole retained history on every open (see the observation-profile row). Cross-version restore, production migration and rollback remain unqualified.

objects.name: Constellation NQ 0.2.0 component package
objects.claim: A Debian package and a tarball for NQ alone, built twice offline with identical bytes and accepted in a clean Debian 12 virtual machine (49 pass, 0 fail, 2 not exercised). It packages one component; it is not an installable Constellation suite. A rebuild of the same source for Ubuntu 22.04 is what the Alpha 2 bundle and the operator-host installation carry; only the Debian 12 assets are published under v0.2.0.
objects.verified_by: the published GitHub release, whose assets were downloaded and checked against their recorded digests and the qualified copies
objects.promotion: NQ's maturity stays developer preview. The package does not qualify any other component or composition. The Ubuntu 22.04 build is published only inside the Alpha 2 bundle, not as a v0.2.0 asset.
